subject: lavvan error "latent variables is not positive definite"

messages.author: 2fe0a16516ab3eb3
messages.subject: lavvan error "latent variables is not positive definite"
parts:
Dear friends, 

I trying to fit lavaan model assuming that there might exists 9 factors in the data set. The data set consists of items from Likart scale 1 to 5. The following is the model. 

la.model <- '
f1 =~ res1+res2+res3+res4+res5
f2 =~ rel1+rel2+rel3+rel4+rel5
f3 =~tan1+tan2+tan3+tan4+tan5
f4 =~ emp1+emp2+emp3+emp4+emp5
f5 =~ cre1+cre2+cre3+cre4+cre5+cre6
f6 =~ court1+court2+court3+court4+court5
f7 =~ sec1+sec2+sec3+sec4+sec5
f8 =~ comp1+comp2+comp3
f9 =~ acc1+acc2+acc3+acc4+acc5'

la.d <- lavaan(la.model, data = d.df)

I got following error message. 

Warning message:
In lavaan::lavaan(model = la.model, data = d.df, model.type = "sem",  :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

I got following results when I inspected. 

> inspect(fit, "cov.lv")
   f1     f2     f3     f4    
f1  0.079                     
f2  0.000 -0.517              
f3  0.000  0.000 -0.046       
f4  0.000  0.000  0.000  0.004

But I am able to get certain output when I use a couple of arguments such as auto.fix.first = TRUE, auto.var = TRUE. 

> la.d
lavaan (0.5-17) converged normally after  45 iterations

  Number of observations                           133

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic             2338.012
  Degrees of freedom                               902
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000

All p-values are zero in summary(fit). I think something is going wrong in my approach. I just followed the way HolzingerSwineford1939 example in lavaan manual. 

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavvan error "latent variables is not positive definite"
parts: But I am able to get certain output when I use a couple of arguments such as auto.fix.first = TRUE, auto.var = TRUE.

Yes, if you fail to specify every single parameter in the syntax, then you can tell lavaan() to estimate or fix certain parameters by default.  Or you can use the cfa() function, which includes those sensible defaults.
All p-values are zero in summary(fit). I think something is going wrong in my approach.

That is not an indication of a problem.  That just means the parameter estimates are far from zero (relative to their SEs) and the model does not fit the data perfectly.
